title: Tiered SLO escalation profiles for canary evacuation
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Problem statement: We've seen canaries that oscillate between passing and failing when simple fixed thresholds are used (esp. p95/p99 latency and tail error rates). This causes noisy rollbacks and unnecessary model churn. We need an automated, explainable escalation system that uses tiered SLO profiles (warning -> degrade -> evacuate) across latency, error rate, token cost, and throughput, with cohort-aware baselining and hysteresis to reduce false positives.
goals: 1) Define and implement 'escalation profiles' that map multi-signal inputs to discrete actions (alert, throttle, reduce weight, full evacuate) during canary/A-B/staged rollouts. 2) Provide per-customer-tier and per-model-family thresholding using quantile-normalized baselines. 3) Integrate with rollout controller to perform safe automated evacuations and provide clear audit trail and operator override. 4) Add synthetic and shadow-test harnesses so thresholds can be validated pre-rollout.
scope:
- New escalation policy objects stored in rollout service config.
- Multi-signal evaluator that handles latency (p50/p95/p99), request error rate, token-cost-per-request regression, and throughput deviation.
- Cohort baselining module computing rolling baselines per customer tier and region.
- Hysteresis, cooldown and escalation timers to prevent thrash.
- Integration points: rollout-api, console alerts, alerting rules (PagerDuty/Slack), and audit log entries.
- E2E test harness that can replay historical traffic and run shadow experiments.
non_goals: - This ticket does not include new ML drift detectors beyond embedding-cosine quick-check tie-breaker. - No changes to billing mechanics; cost signals are advisory for rollback decisions only.
design_decisions:
- Use quantile normalization of latency distributions vs historical baseline rather than fixed-ms thresholds so profiles adapt to model size and sequence length mix.
- Apply weighted scoring across signals: normalized_latency_score (0-1), error_score (0-1), cost_score (0-1), throughput_score (0-1). Escalation thresholds operate on the weighted composite and on per-signal topline checks (e.g., error spikes > X always trumps).
- Three escalation tiers: WARN (emit dashboard alert, no traffic change), SOFT_DEGRADE (reduce canary weight by configured fraction), EVACUATE (route away and roll back to previous stable variant).
- Cohort-aware baselining: compute per-customer-tier baselines and allow global fallback. Baselines use 7d rolling window with outlier trimming.
- Hysteresis: require violation to persist for N consecutive evaluation windows or exceed a statistically significant change-point before escalating.
- Safe fallback: on EVACUATE, route to preconfigured fallback variant of compatible model family.
- Operator override: human-in-the-loop abort and force-evacuate options via console with audit log.
acceptance_criteria:
- Unit tests for signal normalization and scoring logic.
- Integration tests: rollout controller performs SOFT_DEGRADE then EVACUATE under synthetic fault injection.
- Shadow-run: run policy in 'observe-only' mode against last 3 production rollouts; false-positive rate < 3% and true-positive recall > 90% for injected faults.
- Console shows clear timeline (signals, composite score, action taken) and audit log entry for every automated action.
- Runbook updated and on-call notified when EVACUATE occurs.
- Dashboard panels created: composite score heatmap, cohort baselines, recent evacuations with links to PRs and metrics.
risks_and_mitigation:
- Risk: over-eager evacuations causing availability regressions. Mitigation: conservative default profiles, require persistent violation and use soft-degrade before full evacuation.
- Risk: noisy signals from traffic spikes. Mitigation: include throughput-normalized signals and change-point detection.
- Risk: threshold drift making policies useless. Mitigation: add automatic re-calibration job that proposes adjusted profiles and requires manual approval for production rollouts.
- Risk: operator confusion. Mitigation: add clear console UX, explainability fields (which signals triggered), and one-click rollback or resume.
